This is the default configuration for Tiny Tapeout projects. It should fit most designs.
If you change it, please make sure you understand what you are doing. We are not responsible
if your project fails because of a bad configuration.
!!! DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE unless you know what you are doing !!!
If you get stuck with this config, please open an issue or get in touch via the discord.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
Read the SystemVerilog with the slang frontend. LibreLane's default read
(read_verilog -defer) cannot resolve the interfaces that rtu passes down to
its sub-blocks: 'Could not find signal \sh_req.resp_result in rtu'.
Scene SRAM: IHP's RM_IHPSG13_1P_512x16_c2_bm_bist (236.80 x 191.34 um), from the PDK.
Bottom-left corner of the core. Its signal pins are on its bottom edge, so FS
turns them up towards the logic. The tile's I/O pins are on the top edge.
VDD! (periphery) and VDDARRAY! (bit cells) on VPWR, VSS! on VGND.
The tile's PDN is Metal4 stripes only, and the SRAM blocks Metal2-Metal4, so pdngen
stops its stripes at the macro. pdn_cfg.tcl drops LibreLane's empty per-macro grid,
and Project.ExtendPowerStripes (librelane_plugin_tinytracer_pdn.py, odb_stripes.py)
redraws the stripes through the macro on its Metal4 supply columns.
GeneratePDN checks its grid before ExtendPowerStripes connects the SRAM, so its
violation count always includes the unconnected SRAM. OpenROAD's check_power_grid
passes for VPWR and VGND on the design ExtendPowerStripes writes.
Sign-off with the SRAM, as the other CMOS5L SRAM projects do. Magic DRC and its
overlap check misread the SRAM's LEF obstructions (the precheck's KLayout DRC is
the sign-off), and LVS treats the SRAM as a black box (its CDL is not LVS clean).
Configuration docs: https://librelane.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/configuration.html
